main_text.p: est Doctissimi & punctissimi viri mollior hæc sententia: Ego tamen mallem, si absoluté jure, verbi gratia, Me libros in publica Bibliotheca non violaturum, aut in cæteris ejusdem momenti, absq; multâ alicujus mentione: si violarem sub quovis scopo aut prætextu; Mallem (inquam) Deum supplex adire, ut me absolvat à perjurio, quàm ad miserrima deflectere subterfugia, quæ apud viros Cordatos non excusent, quod in cæteris ejusdem ponderis faciendum suadeo.

14 Ista autem de juramentis & perjurio, cùm tam exposita sit doctrina, quid de nobis fiet (Academici) qui tantæ Religionis sacramentum tam negligenter & licenter antehac habuimus; & tam perfidè pergimus profanare? Adeò ut quod Lysander olim effutivit de fide Ethnicorum quorundam Ambulatoria, pueros Astragalis, Reges Juramentis ludere, Christianis quamplurimis non minùs conveniat in hujus sæculi [illegible, ~12 letters] , in quo eam [illegible, ~10 letters]

page.notes: The Greek word in the sentence beginning "Adeò ut" (after "hujus sæculi") is printed in Greek letters but is too smudged to read reliably; I have not guessed it. The final line of the page is faded and only partly legible, so it is marked as illegible rather than completed. Italic and roman boundaries in the body are approximate where the scan is faint. The page is cut off at the foot, so the paragraph continues beyond this scan.
